name: Ford Mustang GT
reliability: 7/10 — robust Coyote V8; hard launches and track use stress the drivetrain
cost_to_own: Insurance: Very High (V8 muscle, ~$2,655/yr avg) · Maintenance ~$710/yr
popular_mods: Supercharger (Roush/Whipple/Procharger) — the big power move, 700+ hp
Sticky tires to tame wheel hop on launches

generations.4th Gen SN95 (1994–2004): 215hp 5.0L pushrod V8 at launch, swapped to 4.6L modular OHC V8 in 1996 (260hp). 'New Edge' facelift in 1999.
generations.5th Gen S197 (2005–2014): 300hp 4.6L V8 (2005–2010). Major upgrade in 2011 with 5.0L Coyote DOHC producing 412hp. First Mustang on its own platform.
generations.6th Gen S550 (2015–2023): 435hp at launch, bumped to 460hp in 2018. First Mustang with independent rear suspension. Available worldwide for the first time.
generations.7th Gen S650 (2024–present): 480–486hp Coyote V8 (with active exhaust). New dual-throttle intake. Most powerful stock GT ever built.

common_issues: IRS half-shaft failure under hard launches (S550+)
Transmission fluid overheating on track (10-speed auto)
Wheel hop with manual on stock tires
maintenance_tips: Upgrade diff and transmission fluid to racing spec if tracking
Check rear axle half-shafts if launching hard regularly
Coolant overflow tank cracks over time — inspect at 50k+

engine.detail: 5.0L Coyote DOHC V8 - Gen3 in this 460 hp / 420 lb-ft trim with dual port + direct injection and a 7,500 rpm redline.
engine.watch: Genuinely robust; just keep the 5W-50 fresh and add cooling for track days, since heat is what stresses these cars.

drivetrain.detail: RWD with a Getrag MT82-D4 6-speed manual or the 10R80 10-speed auto, feeding an independent rear with a limited-slip diff.
drivetrain.watch: The MT82 is notchy with weak synchros and high-rpm 2-3 lockout; hard launches also snap the stock IRS half-shafts.

suspension.detail: First Mustang with independent rear suspension; MagneRide adaptive dampers optional on the Performance Pack.
suspension.watch: Soft rubber IRS subframe bushings let the diff walk, so wheel hop on hard launches is the classic S550 complaint.

brakes.detail: Big Brembo six-piston front calipers on Performance Pack cars haul the ~3,705 lb coupe down hard.
brakes.watch: Strong for the street; on track step up to race pads and high-temp fluid and mind fade on repeat stops.

body.detail: Steel unibody fastback around 3,705 lbs with the S550's fully independent rear packaging.
body.watch: The plastic coolant degas/overflow tank turns brittle and cracks with age - worth inspecting past 50k.
